prize_parts.citation: for the theoretical prediction of the time-reversal-protected quantum spin Hall state and its first experimental observation in HgTe quantum wells, opening the field of topological insulators

statement.case_for: After the full first round my preferred configuration is unchanged: a single part for B013 to Kane, Mele and Molenkamp. Having read the seven other files, I see no scientific objection to B013, only allocation and wording questions, and that is the situation I want when we ask whether a discovery is really groundbreaking. The chain is complete and could have failed at each link: a Z2 invariant protected by time-reversal symmetry (Kane and Mele), a sharp quantitative prediction of edge conductance in a material with inverted bands, and then Molenkamp's measurement of quantised conductance that disappears in wide samples. Nature gave the clue. About eighteen years of independent transport and photoemission work, across several material families, closes the maturity question, which is not true of B021 or B025. In answer to the chair, my one-sentence distinction from 2016 is this: the 2016 prize recognised topological phase transitions and Hall-type phases in model and thin-film systems, whereas this prize recognises a new insulating state of ordinary spin-orbit-coupled materials whose protected edge states follow from time-reversal symmetry and are observed in a real device. I would accept the single-part prize as sufficient. Kroll and Lindroth both name B013 as their first alternative, and I do not think a second part is needed to make the prize complete.
statement.case_against: The allocation remains imperfect, and I would rather say so in the minutes than hide it. The Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang HgTe proposal told Molenkamp where to look, and Zhang is dead, so a decisive link falls outside the credited set. Hasan's 3D ARPES work is an original experiment that turned the idea into a materials field, and any trio excludes someone with a serious claim. Mehlig's point that Fu-Kane-Mele and Moore-Balents theory sits behind the 3D branch shows that adding Hasan would open a second incomplete attribution rather than close the first. The overlap with 2016 is a matter of wording, but it is a real matter, and a citation that says 'a new class of matter' invites the 3D branch into the claim. That is why I have narrowed my round-1 wording: the citation now ends on the quantum spin Hall state and its observation, and mentions the field only as what it opened. I also accept Kroll's point that practical devices are scarce, but the statutes ask for a discovery, not a technology. The weakness of my second-ranked option B008 remains the one-name credit.

responses.point: Eriksson's round-1 file keeps Kane, Mele and Molenkamp but says that Hasan's ARPES work is a decisive second experimental strand and that the 2D and 3D branches may be hard to separate.
responses.response: I now think we agree on the allocation, and I am glad you moved off the Mele-for-Hasan swap, which I could not support. I take your 3D concern seriously and do not want it treated as minor. My answer is that the 2D and 3D branches can be separated for the purposes of a citation, because the 2D case has the complete loop of prediction, quantitative test and independent replication, while the 3D case rests on a second theory strand (Fu-Kane-Mele, Moore-Balents) that is not among the credited names. If you still think the committee should name the 3D materials class in the text, tell me which words you would use that do not claim Hasan's work for the trio. Otherwise I would record the omission as an allocation judgment.

responses.point: Mehlig argues that adding Hasan would open a second incomplete attribution because the 3D branch rests on Fu-Kane-Mele and Moore-Balents theory that is not credited, and prefers a citation centred on the quantum spin Hall effect.
responses.response: This is the most useful argument in the round for me, and it changes my own wording. In round 1 I ended the citation on topological insulators as a new class of matter, which does lean towards the 3D branch. I have now narrowed the citation to the time-reversal-protected quantum spin Hall state and its first observation, and I mention the field only as something it opened. I also want to adopt your sharper statement of the 2016 distinction, symmetry-protected band topology in spin-orbit-coupled materials, with the caveat that the Hall-conductance language of 2016 should not be allowed to blur it. One point of difference: I would not say that the HgTe measurement settles the spin-polarised nature of the edge, which Johansson rightly says has been debated, so the citation should speak of edge conduction and not of spin transport.

responses.point: Pearce, as chair, says the citation should not state that Kane and Mele predicted the HgTe effect because the BHZ proposal guided Molenkamp, and asks whether the 2016 overlap is a real obstacle or only a point for citation wording.
responses.response: I agree with your wording point and have built it into the citation: it names the prediction of the quantum spin Hall state, not of the HgTe realisation, and it says 'first experimental observation' without saying who suggested the material. On your 2016 question I think it is a wording obstacle and not a scientific one, and a citation that states the symmetry-protected edge states clearly passes it. I also thank you for accepting that B008 cannot lead on its present credit. You asked me earlier about a second part with a widened credit. I cannot find a defensible multi-person credit for B008 in the names we have, so I do not propose it as a second part, and I would keep it only as an alternative, though I remain convinced the diffuse neutrino flux is a real clue from the sky.

responses.point: Kroll keeps B006 for Katori and Ye as his preferred part, with a clean two-name attribution and a closed loop of clock comparisons between independent laboratories, and names B013 as his first alternative.
responses.response: I take the clock comparisons seriously. They are as independent a confirmation as an instrument can have, and the attribution is the cleanest on the list. I also accept your point that Eriksson's swap would penalise the original proposal, since you made it independently of me. My reason for not moving to B006 is the one you give yourself: the discovery claim is partly prospective until the second is redefined, and I could not write a citation sentence about a new state or new law of nature, whereas for B013 I can. Since you name B013 as your first alternative, I would ask whether the single part is acceptable to you, and I would not ask for a second part solely to include the clocks. If the redefinition of the second takes place, I would want this case reviewed on its merits in a later year.

responses.point: Olsson asks for the weight on theory to be matched by the HgTe measurement, since a prediction alone would not satisfy her, and keeps Molenkamp as the experimental anchor over Hasan.
responses.response: I agree, and it is the reason I keep Molenkamp in all versions of my configuration. The HgTe experiment was a test that could have failed: quantised edge conduction, gate dependence and the breakdown in wide samples all had to come out right. Your suggestion that Hasan's case be handled as a separate later conversation is the right one, and I would add that the committee should then ask whether the 3D prize is a distinct achievement with its own credited names, including the theorists behind it, and not a supplement to this one.

uncertainties: Whether a citation that is accurate for the three named people can still honestly describe the field they started without overclaiming the 3D branch, Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang and Fu-Kane-Mele.

Whether outside experts would consider the 2016 distinction (symmetry-protected band topology in real spin-orbit materials versus topological phase transitions) as clear as the committee does. As Secretary I would want an external report on this before the vote.
My knowledge of exact priority details comes from the discussion and from memory, and I have not checked them against the primary papers.
Whether B008 can ever be credited fairly with a named multi-person set, which I cannot verify from the files I have been given.
statement.conflict_note: No change since round 1. I have no connection to any credited person in the shortlisted candidates. My supervisor and frequent co-author are string and gravity theorists unconnected to these ballots. I did rank B008 first in my opening and have moved off it, so I disclose that prior preference. As Secretary I would want external reports for any contested allocation.
